---------------------------- MODULE W4Od3m0p6t4 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Banks, MaxVer

VARIABLES ledgerVer, committed, authorized, pending

vars == <<ledgerVer, committed, authorized, pending>>

Entry(b, v) == [bank |-> b, ver |-> v]

TypeOK ==
    /\ ledgerVer \in 0..MaxVer
    /\ committed \subseteq [bank : Banks, ver : 0..MaxVer]
    /\ pending \subseteq [bank : Banks, ver : 0..MaxVer]
    /\ authorized \subseteq Banks

Init ==
    /\ ledgerVer = 0
    /\ committed = {}
    /\ authorized = {}
    /\ pending = {}

Register(b) ==
    /\ b \notin authorized
    /\ authorized' = authorized \cup {b}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ledgerVer, committed, pending>>

Suspend(b) ==
    /\ b \in authorized
    /\ authorized' = authorized \ {b}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ledgerVer, committed, pending>>

Submit(b) ==
    /\ b \in authorized
    /\ Entry(b, ledgerVer) \notin pending
    /\ pending' = pending \cup {Entry(b, ledgerVer)}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ledgerVer, committed, authorized>>

Commit(p) ==
    /\ p \in pending
    /\ p.bank \in authorized
    /\ p.ver = ledgerVer
    /\ ledgerVer < MaxVer
    /\ ledgerVer' = ledgerVer + 1
    /\ committed' = committed \cup {p}
    /\ pending' = pending \ {p}
    /\ UNCHANGED authorized

Retry(p) ==
    /\ p \in pending
    /\ p.ver # ledgerVer
    /\ pending' = (pending \ {p}) \cup {Entry(p.bank, ledgerVer)}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ledgerVer, committed, authorized>>

Next ==
    \/ \E b \in Banks : Register(b)
    \/ \E b \in Banks : Suspend(b)
    \/ \E b \in Banks : Submit(b)
    \/ \E p \in pending : Commit(p)
    \/ \E p \in pending : Retry(p)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

NoStaleCommit == \A c \in committed : c.ver < ledgerVer
============================================================================

CONSTANTS
    Banks = {b1, b2}
    MaxVer = 3
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoStaleCommit
nl:
An interbank settlement batch is applied against a shared ledger that carries a monotonically increasing version number. Member banks submit settlement instructions, but each instruction records the ledger version the bank observed when it prepared the instruction. The controller uses optimistic locking: an instruction may commit only if the version it observed still equals the current ledger version, and each successful commit bumps the ledger version by one. If an instruction's observed version has fallen behind, it is stale and must be retried against the fresh version rather than committed. Separately, the set of authorized banks changes at runtime as members join or are suspended, and only a currently authorized bank may submit or commit. The controller must guarantee that the committed record never contains a stale application: every committed entry must reflect a version strictly older than the ledger has since advanced to.
SAFETY PROPERTY: No committed settlement entry carries a version equal to or greater than the current ledger version, so no stale or superseded lock was ever committed.

---------------------------- MODULE W4Od13m8p5t1 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Agents, Machines, Slots, MaxTok

VARIABLES coarse, fine, queue, done, nextTok

vars == <<coarse, fine, queue, done, nextTok>>

NONE == "none"

TypeOK ==
    /\ coarse \in [Machines -> Agents \cup {NONE}]
    /\ fine \subseteq [mch : Machines, slot : Slots, owner : Agents]
    /\ queue \subseteq [mch : Machines, slot : Slots, owner : Agents]
    /\ done \subseteq [mch : Machines, slot : Slots, tok : 1..MaxTok]
    /\ nextTok \in 1..(MaxTok + 1)

Init ==
    /\ coarse = [m \in Machines |-> NONE]
    /\ fine = {}
    /\ queue = {}
    /\ done = {}
    /\ nextTok = 1

TakeCoarse(a, m) ==
    /\ coarse[m] = NONE
    /\ coarse' = [coarse EXCEPT ![m] = a]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<fine, queue, done, nextTok>>

ReleaseCoarse(m) ==
    /\ coarse[m] # NONE
    /\ coarse' = [coarse EXCEPT ![m] = NONE]
    /\ fine' = {f \in fine : f.mch # m}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, done, nextTok>>

TakeFine(a, m, s) ==
    /\ coarse[m] = a
    /\ [mch |-> m, slot |-> s, owner |-> a] \notin fine
    /\ fine' = fine \cup {[mch |-> m, slot |-> s, owner |-> a]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, queue, done, nextTok>>

Enqueue(a, m, s) ==
    /\ [mch |-> m, slot |-> s, owner |-> a] \in fine
    /\ [mch |-> m, slot |-> s, owner |-> a] \notin queue
    /\ queue' = queue \cup {[mch |-> m, slot |-> s, owner |-> a]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, fine, done, nextTok>>

Dispense(c) ==
    /\ c \in queue
    /\ nextTok <= MaxTok
    /\ \A d \in done : ~(d.mch = c.mch /\ d.slot = c.slot)
    /\ done' = done \cup {[mch |-> c.mch, slot |-> c.slot, tok |-> nextTok]}
    /\ nextTok' = nextTok + 1
    /\ queue' = queue \ {c}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, fine>>

Next ==
    \/ \E a \in Agents, m \in Machines : TakeCoarse(a, m)
    \/ \E m \in Machines : ReleaseCoarse(m)
    \/ \E a \in Agents, m \in Machines, s \in Slots : TakeFine(a, m, s)
    \/ \E a \in Agents, m \in Machines, s \in Slots : Enqueue(a, m, s)
    \/ \E c \in queue : Dispense(c)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

AtMostOnceDispense ==
    \A d1, d2 \in done :
        (d1.mch = d2.mch /\ d1.slot = d2.slot) => d1.tok = d2.tok
============================================================================
nl:
A vending machine network dispenses prepaid orders, where each dispense is physically irreversible: once a can drops it cannot be un-dropped. To coordinate, an agent must first take a coarse lock on the whole machine, then a fine lock on the specific slot, following the coarse-then-fine hierarchy. Only after holding both locks may it enqueue a dispense command. Dispense commands travel over a network that may deliver them in any order, so a command may arrive well after it was issued. When a dispense command is finally delivered, the machine dispenses the slot only if that exact slot has not already been dispensed, stamping each physical dispense with a unique monotonically increasing token. Locks can also be released so the machine is never permanently stuck. Because the same slot could be commanded more than once through reordering or retries, the network must ensure a slot is never physically dispensed twice.
SAFETY PROPERTY: For any slot, all recorded dispense events carry the same token, meaning the irreversible dispense of a given slot happened at most once.

---------------------------- MODULE W4Od2m0p1t0 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Robots, MaxVer

VARIABLES version, value, pend, applied

vars == <<version, value, pend, applied>>

NONE == [seenVer |-> 99, want |-> 0]

TypeOK ==
    /\ version \in 0..MaxVer
    /\ value \in 0..MaxVer
    /\ pend \in [Robots -> ([seenVer : 0..MaxVer, want : 1..MaxVer] \cup {NONE})]
    /\ applied \subseteq [robot : Robots, atVer : 0..MaxVer]

Init ==
    /\ version = 0
    /\ value = 0
    /\ pend = [r \in Robots |-> NONE]
    /\ applied = {}

Read(r, w) ==
    /\ pend[r] = NONE
    /\ pend' = [pend EXCEPT ![r] = [seenVer |-> version, want |-> w]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<version, value, applied>>

Crash(r) ==
    /\ pend[r] # NONE
    /\ pend' = [pend EXCEPT ![r] = NONE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<version, value, applied>>

Write(r) ==
    /\ pend[r] # NONE
    /\ pend[r].seenVer = version
    /\ version < MaxVer
    /\ version' = version + 1
    /\ value' = pend[r].want
    /\ applied' = applied \cup {[robot |-> r, atVer |-> version]}
    /\ pend' = [pend EXCEPT ![r] = NONE]

Retry(r) ==
    /\ pend[r] # NONE
    /\ pend[r].seenVer # version
    /\ pend' = [pend EXCEPT ![r] = [seenVer |-> version, want |-> pend[r].want]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<version, value, applied>>

Next ==
    \/ \E r \in Robots, w \in 1..MaxVer : Read(r, w)
    \/ \E r \in Robots : Crash(r)
    \/ \E r \in Robots : Write(r)
    \/ \E r \in Robots : Retry(r)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

NoLostUpdate ==
    \A w1, w2 \in applied : (w1.atVer = w2.atVer) => (w1.robot = w2.robot)
============================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Robots = {r1, r2}
    MaxVer = 3
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoLostUpdate
nl:
A warehouse robot fleet shares a single inventory record that tracks the count of a part on a shelf. Each robot reads the current value together with a version stamp, computes a new value, and writes it back using optimistic concurrency: the write succeeds only if the version stamp it read still matches the record's current version, and a successful write bumps the version. A robot whose stamp is out of date has been beaten to the write by another robot and must reread and retry rather than clobber the newer value. Robots can crash silently at any point, discarding whatever read they were holding, so pending reads must never be assumed to complete. The system logs every applied write together with the version it produced. To be correct, the shared record must never lose an update: each committed version must have been produced by exactly one applied write, so no robot's committed change is silently overwritten.
SAFETY PROPERTY: No two distinct applied writes were committed at the same record version, so every accepted update advanced the record without being lost.

VARIABLES inZone, ver, req, entered

    /\ inZone \subseteq Trains
    /\ ver \in 0..MaxVer
    /\ req \in [Trains -> 0..MaxVer \cup {NONE}]
    /\ entered \subseteq [train : Trains, atVer : 0..MaxVer]

    /\ ver = 0
    /\ req = [t \in Trains |-> NONE]

    /\ req[t] = ver
    /\ t \notin inZone
    /\ Cardinality(inZone) < Cap
    /\ ver < MaxVer
    /\ inZone' = inZone \cup {t}
    /\ ver' = ver + 1
    /\ entered' = entered \cup {[train |-> t, atVer |-> ver]}
    /\ req' = [req EXCEPT ![t] = NONE]

Retry(t) ==
    /\ req[t] # NONE
    /\ req[t] # ver
    /\ req' = [req EXCEPT ![t] = ver]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<inZone, ver, entered>>

Leave(t) ==

    /\ inZone' = inZone \ {t}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ver, req, entered>>

Crash(t) ==
    /\ req[t] # NONE
    /\ req' = [req EXCEPT ![t] = NONE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<inZone, ver, entered>>

    \/ \E t \in Trains : Enter(t)
    \/ \E t \in Trains : Retry(t)
    \/ \E t \in Trains : Leave(t)
    \/ \E t \in Trains : Crash(t)

    Cap = 2
    MaxVer = 4

NEXT Next

nl:
A subway signalling system controls entry into a shared track zone that can safely hold only a bounded number of trains at once. Each train that wants to enter first reads the zone's current occupancy version, then attempts to commit its entry using optimistic locking: the entry is accepted only if the version it read still matches the live version, and every accepted entry bumps the version. If a train's read is stale it must retry against the fresh version. A train inside the zone may leave, freeing space. Trains can also crash silently before entering, abandoning a pending entry request that then simply disappears without ever occupying the zone. The signalling logic must guarantee that the number of trains simultaneously inside the shared zone never exceeds the physical capacity.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of trains occupying the shared track zone is always less than or equal to the fixed capacity.

---------------------------- MODULE W4Od10m9p3t4 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Trains, Berths, MaxEpoch

VARIABLES epoch, owner, holds, inService

vars == <<epoch, owner, holds, inService>>

NONE == "none"

TypeOK ==
    /\ epoch \in 0..MaxEpoch
    /\ owner \in [Berths -> Trains \cup {NONE}]
    /\ holds \in [Trains -> SUBSET Berths]
    /\ inService \subseteq Berths

Init ==
    /\ epoch = 0
    /\ owner = [b \in Berths |-> NONE]
    /\ holds = [t \in Trains |-> {}]
    /\ inService = Berths

Reconfigure(newSvc) ==
    /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
    /\ newSvc # {}
    /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ inService' = newSvc
    /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, holds>>

Allocate(t, b) ==
    /\ b \in inService
    /\ owner[b] = NONE
    /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![b] = t]
    /\ holds' = [holds EXCEPT ![t] = holds[t] \cup {b}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, inService>>

Release(t, b) ==
    /\ b \in holds[t]
    /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![b] = NONE]
    /\ holds' = [holds EXCEPT ![t] = holds[t] \ {b}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, inService>>

Handover(t1, t2, b) ==
    /\ t1 # t2
    /\ b \in holds[t1]
    /\ owner[b] = t1
    /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![b] = t2]
    /\ holds' = [holds EXCEPT ![t1] = holds[t1] \ {b}, ![t2] = holds[t2] \cup {b}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, inService>>

Next ==
    \/ \E s \in (SUBSET Berths) \ {{}} : Reconfigure(s)
    \/ \E t \in Trains, b \in Berths : Allocate(t, b)
    \/ \E t \in Trains, b \in Berths : Release(t, b)
    \/ \E t1, t2 \in Trains, b \in Berths : Handover(t1, t2, b)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

OwnershipAgrees ==
    \A b \in Berths, t \in Trains :
        (owner[b] = t) <=> (b \in holds[t])
============================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Trains = {t1, t2}
    Berths = {b1, b2}
    MaxEpoch = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT OwnershipAgrees
nl:
A subway signalling system allocates numbered platform berths to trains under a controller that reconfigures the line in numbered epochs. Each reconfiguration bumps the epoch and changes which berths are currently in service, so the set of usable berths grows and shrinks at runtime. A train is allocated a berth only if that berth is currently in service and unowned, and the allocation is recorded from two directions: the berth records its owning train and the train records the berth in the set it holds. A train may release a berth it holds, clearing both records together, or hand a berth it owns directly over to another train, moving both records atomically. The danger is a double allocation, where the berth-to-owner record and the train-to-held record disagree so that two trains believe they hold the same berth. The controller must keep the two directions of the ownership records in perfect agreement.
SAFETY PROPERTY: A berth records a train as its owner if and only if that train records the berth among the berths it holds, so no berth is ever doubly allocated.

---------------------------- MODULE W4Od2m6p2t2 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Robots, Units, LeaseDur, MaxClock

VARIABLES freeUnits, leases, clock, pending

vars == <<freeUnits, leases, clock, pending>>

Held == {l.unit : l \in leases}

TypeOK ==
    /\ freeUnits \subseteq Units
    /\ leases \subseteq [unit : Units, robot : Robots, exp : 0..(MaxClock + LeaseDur)]
    /\ clock \in 0..MaxClock
    /\ pending \subseteq [robot : Robots, unit : Units]

Init ==
    /\ freeUnits = Units
    /\ leases = {}
    /\ clock = 0
    /\ pending = {}

Request(r, u) ==
    /\ [robot |-> r, unit |-> u] \notin pending
    /\ pending' = pending \cup {[robot |-> r, unit |-> u]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<freeUnits, leases, clock>>

Grant(p) ==
    /\ p \in pending
    /\ p.unit \in freeUnits
    /\ freeUnits' = freeUnits \ {p.unit}
    /\ leases' = leases \cup {[unit |-> p.unit, robot |-> p.robot, exp |-> clock + LeaseDur]}
    /\ pending' = pending \ {p}
    /\ UNCHANGED clock

Return(l) ==
    /\ l \in leases
    /\ freeUnits' = freeUnits \cup {l.unit}
    /\ leases' = leases \ {l}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, pending>>

Tick ==
    /\ clock < MaxClock
    /\ clock' = clock + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<freeUnits, leases, pending>>

Expire(l) ==
    /\ l \in leases
    /\ l.exp <= clock
    /\ freeUnits' = freeUnits \cup {l.unit}
    /\ leases' = leases \ {l}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, pending>>

Next ==
    \/ \E r \in Robots, u \in Units : Request(r, u)
    \/ \E p \in pending : Grant(p)
    \/ \E l \in leases : Return(l)
    \/ Tick
    \/ \E l \in leases : Expire(l)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

Conservation ==
    /\ freeUnits \cup Held = Units
    /\ freeUnits \cap Held = {}
============================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Robots = {r1, r2}
    Units = {u1, u2}
    LeaseDur = 2
    MaxClock = 3
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT Conservation
nl:
A warehouse robot fleet draws interchangeable battery units from a single shared pool, and two independent dispatcher instances both hand out the same pool, so nothing may be created or destroyed behind their backs. A robot first files a request naming a specific free unit, and a dispatcher may grant it by moving that unit out of the free pool into a time-limited lease stamped with an expiry drawn from a shared clock. A robot may voluntarily return a leased unit to the pool. The shared clock advances in ticks, and any lease whose expiry has passed is reclaimed, returning its unit to the free pool. The essential invariant of the shared pool is conservation: every battery unit is either sitting free in the pool or held in exactly one live lease, and the two sets together always account for every unit with no overlap.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The free pool and the set of leased units together partition the full set of battery units, so no unit is ever duplicated or lost.

---------------------------- MODULE W4Od19m4p4t3 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Patrons, QMax, Copies

VARIABLES queue, granted, slow, refused

vars == <<queue, granted, slow, refused>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ queue \in Seq(Patrons)
    /\ Len(queue) <= QMax
    /\ granted \subseteq Patrons
    /\ slow \in BOOLEAN
    /\ refused \subseteq Patrons

Init ==
    /\ queue = <<>>
    /\ granted = {}
    /\ slow = FALSE
    /\ refused = {}

Enqueue(p) ==
    /\ Len(queue) < QMax
    /\ queue' = Append(queue, p)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<granted, slow, refused>>

Backpressure(p) ==
    /\ Len(queue) = QMax
    /\ refused' = refused \cup {p}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, granted, slow>>

Grant ==
    /\ ~slow
    /\ Len(queue) > 0
    /\ Head(queue) \notin granted
    /\ Cardinality(granted) < Copies
    /\ granted' = granted \cup {Head(queue)}
    /\ queue' = Tail(queue)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<slow, refused>>

Skip ==
    /\ ~slow
    /\ Len(queue) > 0
    /\ (Head(queue) \in granted \/ Cardinality(granted) >= Copies)
    /\ queue' = Tail(queue)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<granted, slow, refused>>

Return(p) ==
    /\ p \in granted
    /\ granted' = granted \ {p}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, slow, refused>>

SetSlow(b) ==
    /\ slow # b
    /\ slow' = b
    /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, granted, refused>>

Next ==
    \/ \E p \in Patrons : Enqueue(p)
    \/ \E p \in Patrons : Backpressure(p)
    \/ Grant
    \/ Skip
    \/ \E p \in Patrons : Return(p)
    \/ \E b \in BOOLEAN : SetSlow(b)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

CapacityOK ==
    /\ Len(queue) <= QMax
    /\ Cardinality(granted) <= Copies
============================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Patrons = {p1, p2}
    QMax = 2
    Copies = 1
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT CapacityOK
nl:
A library book reservation service feeds incoming reservation requests through a bounded work queue with backpressure. New requests may be appended only while the queue is below its maximum length; when the queue is full, backpressure blocks further appends until the worker drains one, and any patron turned away while the queue is full is recorded in a refused set. A single worker pulls the head request and, if a copy of the book is available, grants the reservation to that patron and consumes a copy. A patron may later return the book, freeing a copy again. The worker can be slow: it may enter a stalled state and later resume, so processing is delayed but never permanently failed. Two limits must always hold: the pending queue can never grow past its bound, and the number of outstanding granted reservations can never exceed the number of physical copies.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The pending queue length never exceeds its maximum and the number of outstanding reservations never exceeds the number of copies.

---------------------------- MODULE W4Od8m0p4t1 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Students, Courses, Seats, MaxVer

VARIABLES enrolled, ver, inbox, rejected

vars == <<enrolled, ver, inbox, rejected>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ enrolled \in [Courses -> SUBSET Students]
    /\ ver \in [Courses -> 0..MaxVer]
    /\ inbox \subseteq [stu : Students, crs : Courses, seen : 0..MaxVer]
    /\ rejected \subseteq [stu : Students, crs : Courses, seen : 0..MaxVer]

Init ==
    /\ enrolled = [c \in Courses |-> {}]
    /\ ver = [c \in Courses |-> 0]
    /\ inbox = {}
    /\ rejected = {}

Submit(s, c) ==
    /\ s \notin enrolled[c]
    /\ [stu |-> s, crs |-> c, seen |-> ver[c]] \notin inbox
    /\ inbox' = inbox \cup {[stu |-> s, crs |-> c, seen |-> ver[c]]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<enrolled, ver, rejected>>

Commit(m) ==
    /\ m \in inbox
    /\ m.seen = ver[m.crs]
    /\ m.stu \notin enrolled[m.crs]
    /\ Cardinality(enrolled[m.crs]) < Seats
    /\ ver[m.crs] < MaxVer
    /\ enrolled' = [enrolled EXCEPT ![m.crs] = enrolled[m.crs] \cup {m.stu}]
    /\ ver' = [ver EXCEPT ![m.crs] = ver[m.crs] + 1]
    /\ inbox' = inbox \ {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED rejected

RejectStale(m) ==
    /\ m \in inbox
    /\ m.seen # ver[m.crs]
    /\ inbox' = inbox \ {m}
    /\ rejected' = rejected \cup {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<enrolled, ver>>

Drop(s, c) ==
    /\ s \in enrolled[c]
    /\ enrolled' = [enrolled EXCEPT ![c] = enrolled[c] \ {s}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ver, inbox, rejected>>

Recycle(c) ==
    /\ ver[c] = MaxVer
    /\ ver' = [ver EXCEPT ![c] = 0]
    /\ inbox' = {m \in inbox : m.crs # c}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<enrolled, rejected>>

Next ==
    \/ \E s \in Students, c \in Courses : Submit(s, c)
    \/ \E m \in inbox : Commit(m)
    \/ \E m \in inbox : RejectStale(m)
    \/ \E s \in Students, c \in Courses : Drop(s, c)
    \/ \E c \in Courses : Recycle(c)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

SeatsRespected == \A c \in Courses : Cardinality(enrolled[c]) <= Seats
============================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Students = {s1, s2}
    Courses = {c1}
    Seats = 1
    MaxVer = 3
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT SeatsRespected
nl:
A university course-registration system enrolls students into courses that each have a bounded number of seats. A student submits an enrollment message stamped with the enrollment version it observed for that course, using optimistic locking. Confirmation messages travel over a network that may reorder them, so messages are held in an unordered buffer and applied in any order. When a message is applied, the enrollment commits only if its stamped version still matches the course's current version and a seat remains free, in which case the student is enrolled and the course version bumps. A message whose stamped version is stale is rejected rather than committed. A student may also drop the course, freeing a seat, and the registrar periodically rolls a course's version counter back to zero once it saturates, discarding that course's stale in-flight messages. The registrar must guarantee that no course ever holds more enrolled students than it has seats.
SAFETY PROPERTY: For every course, the number of enrolled students never exceeds the number of seats.

---------------------------- MODULE W4Od9m9p0t1 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Controllers, MaxEpoch

VARIABLES epoch, key, active, inbox

vars == <<epoch, key, active, inbox>>

NONE == "none"

TypeOK ==
    /\ epoch \in 0..MaxEpoch
    /\ key \in Controllers \cup {NONE}
    /\ active \subseteq Controllers
    /\ inbox \subseteq [ctrl : Controllers, ep : 0..MaxEpoch]

Init ==
    /\ epoch = 0
    /\ key = NONE
    /\ active = {}
    /\ inbox = {}

IssueGrant(c) ==
    /\ [ctrl |-> c, ep |-> epoch] \notin inbox
    /\ inbox' = inbox \cup {[ctrl |-> c, ep |-> epoch]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, key, active>>

Acquire(m) ==
    /\ m \in inbox
    /\ m.ep = epoch
    /\ key = NONE
    /\ key' = m.ctrl
    /\ active' = active \cup {m.ctrl}
    /\ inbox' = inbox \ {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED epoch

Release ==
    /\ key # NONE
    /\ active' = active \ {key}

    /\ pending' = pending \cup {[bank |-> b, ep |-> epoch]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, authorized, committed>>

Commit(p) ==
    /\ p \in pending
    /\ p.bank \in authorized
    /\ p.ep = epoch
    /\ committed' = committed \cup {p}
    /\ pending' = pending \ {p}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, authorized>>

Crash(p) ==
    /\ p \in pending
    /\ pending' = pending \ {p}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, authorized, committed>>

Next ==
    \/ \E s \in (SUBSET Banks) \ {{}} : Reconfigure(s)
    \/ \E b \in Banks : Submit(b)
    \/ \E p \in pending : Commit(p)
    \/ \E p \in pending : Crash(p)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

PendingClean ==
    \A p \in pending : (p.bank \in authorized) /\ (p.ep = epoch)

CONSTANTS
    Banks = {b1, b2}
    MaxEpoch = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT PendingClean
nl:
A bank's interbank settlement batch admits instructions only from currently authorized member banks, and authorization is managed in numbered epochs. A reconfiguration bumps the epoch and installs a fresh set of authorized banks, and because credentials from an old epoch are worthless, every reconfiguration invalidates all in-flight instructions from the previous epoch. An authorized bank may submit an instruction, which enters the pending set stamped with the current epoch. A pending instruction may commit, moving into the committed ledger, but only while its bank is still authorized and its stamp still matches the live epoch. A bank may crash silently, and its pending instruction simply vanishes. The controller must maintain the discipline that the pending set never contains an instruction from an unauthorized bank or from a stale epoch, so no unauthorized or stale participant can slip an action through.
SAFETY PROPERTY: Every pending instruction is stamped with the current epoch and belongs to a currently authorized bank, so no stale or unauthorized instruction ever lingers awaiting commit.

    /\ fine \in [Drawers -> Pharmacists \cup {NONE}]

    /\ fine = [d \in Drawers |-> NONE]
    /\ dispensing = [d \in Drawers |-> NONE]
    /\ slow = FALSE

TakeCoarse(ph, c) ==
    /\ coarse[c] = NONE
    /\ coarse' = [coarse EXCEPT ![c] = ph]

TakeFine(ph, d) ==

    /\ fine[d] = NONE
    /\ fine' = [fine EXCEPT ![d] = ph]

Begin(ph, d) ==
    /\ ~slow
    /\ fine[d] = ph
    /\ coarse[d.cab] = ph
    /\ dispensing[d] = NONE
    /\ dispensing' = [dispensing EXCEPT ![d] = ph]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, fine, slow>>

Finish(d) ==
    /\ dispensing[d] # NONE
    /\ dispensing' = [dispensing EXCEPT ![d] = NONE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, fine, slow>>

ReleaseFine(d) ==
    /\ fine[d] # NONE
    /\ dispensing[d] = NONE
    /\ fine' = [fine EXCEPT ![d] = NONE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, dispensing, slow>>

ReleaseCoarse(c) ==

    /\ \A d \in Drawers : (d.cab = c) => (fine[d] = NONE)
    /\ coarse' = [coarse EXCEPT ![c] = NONE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<fine, dispensing, slow>>

    /\ slow' = b
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, fine, dispensing>>

    \/ \E ph \in Pharmacists, d \in Drawers : TakeFine(ph, d)
    \/ \E ph \in Pharmacists, d \in Drawers : Begin(ph, d)
    \/ \E d \in Drawers : Finish(d)
    \/ \E d \in Drawers : ReleaseFine(d)
    \/ \E c \in Cabinets : ReleaseCoarse(c)

A pharmacy prescription dispenser guards controlled-substance drawers, where each drawer sits inside a cabinet. To dispense from a drawer a pharmacist must observe the coarse-then-fine locking hierarchy: first take the cabinet's coarse lock, then the specific drawer's fine lock, and only then may the pharmacist begin dispensing at that drawer, which is the mutually exclusive critical section. A pharmacist may finish dispensing, release the drawer's fine lock, and release the cabinet's coarse lock. A pharmacist can be slow, entering a stalled state in which it will not begin a new dispense until it resumes, so dispensing is delayed but the pharmacist never fails. The safety-critical requirement is mutual exclusion of each drawer: a pharmacist may be dispensing at a drawer only while it genuinely holds both that drawer's fine lock and the enclosing cabinet's coarse lock, which guarantees no two pharmacists ever dispense from the same drawer at once.
SAFETY PROPERTY: Whenever a pharmacist is dispensing at a drawer, that pharmacist holds both the drawer's fine lock and its cabinet's coarse lock, so at most one pharmacist ever dispenses from a drawer.

A container-ship crane yard hands out short-term leases on a shared block of stacking capacity, where at most a fixed number of leases may be live at once. A crane first files a request, which enters an unordered request buffer; because the yard's messaging is unreliable, requests are served in any order, not the order filed. The yard grants a request by turning it into a live lease stamped with an expiry time drawn from a shared clock, but only while the number of currently live leases is below the capacity bound. A crane may voluntarily return its lease, and the shared clock advances in ticks so that any lease whose expiry has passed is swept away as expired. Each grant is also recorded in a history log. The controlling requirement is that the number of simultaneously live leases never exceeds the capacity bound.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of currently live leases is always less than or equal to the fixed capacity bound.

A flight may release its slot, returning the token to the free pool, and the shared clock advances in ticks so any lease past its expiry is reclaimed, also returning its token. The number of usable runways is reconfigured at runtime as runways open and close for weather, changing how many leases may be active, but this never creates or destroys landing-slot tokens. SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of free landing-slot tokens plus the number of leased tokens always equals the fixed total number of tokens.

---------------------------- MODULE W4Od2m8p4t5 ----------------------------

CONSTANTS Robots, Zones, Aisles, Cap

ZoneAisles == {[zone |-> z, ai |-> a] : z \in Zones, a \in Aisles}

TypeOK ==

    /\ fineLock \in [ZoneAisles -> Robots \cup {NONE}]
    /\ occupancy \in [ZoneAisles -> SUBSET Robots]
    /\ overrides \subseteq [robot : Robots, kind : {"admit", "evict"}]

Init ==
    /\ zoneLock = [z \in Zones |-> NONE]
    /\ fineLock = [w \in ZoneAisles |-> NONE]
    /\ occupancy = [w \in ZoneAisles |-> {}]
    /\ overrides = {}

TakeZone(r, z) ==
    /\ zoneLock[z] = NONE
    /\ zoneLock' = [zoneLock EXCEPT ![z] = r]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<fineLock, occupancy, overrides>>

TakeFine(r, w) ==
    /\ zoneLock[w.zone] = r
    /\ fineLock[w] = NONE
    /\ fineLock' = [fineLock EXCEPT ![w] = r]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<zoneLock, occupancy, overrides>>

Enter(r, w) ==
    /\ fineLock[w] = r
    /\ zoneLock[w.zone] = r
    /\ r \notin occupancy[w]
    /\ Cardinality(occupancy[w]) < Cap
    /\ occupancy' = [occupancy EXCEPT ![w] = occupancy[w] \cup {r}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<zoneLock, fineLock, overrides>>

Leave(r, w) ==
    /\ r \in occupancy[w]
    /\ occupancy' = [occupancy EXCEPT ![w] = occupancy[w] \ {r}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<zoneLock, fineLock, overrides>>

ReleaseFine(w) ==
    /\ fineLock[w] # NONE
    /\ fineLock' = [fineLock EXCEPT ![w] = NONE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<zoneLock, occupancy, overrides>>

ReleaseZone(z) ==
    /\ zoneLock[z] # NONE
    /\ \A w \in ZoneAisles : (w.zone = z) => (fineLock[w] = NONE)
    /\ zoneLock' = [zoneLock EXCEPT ![z] = NONE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<fineLock, occupancy, overrides>>

AdminAdmit(r, w) ==
    /\ r \notin occupancy[w]
    /\ Cardinality(occupancy[w]) < Cap
    /\ occupancy' = [occupancy EXCEPT ![w] = occupancy[w] \cup {r}]
    /\ overrides' = overrides \cup {[robot |-> r, kind |-> "admit"]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<zoneLock, fineLock>>

AdminEvict(r, w) ==
    /\ r \in occupancy[w]
    /\ occupancy' = [occupancy EXCEPT ![w] = occupancy[w] \ {r}]
    /\ overrides' = overrides \cup {[robot |-> r, kind |-> "evict"]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<zoneLock, fineLock>>

Next ==
    \/ \E r \in Robots, z \in Zones : TakeZone(r, z)
    \/ \E r \in Robots, w \in ZoneAisles : TakeFine(r, w)
    \/ \E r \in Robots, w \in ZoneAisles : Enter(r, w)
    \/ \E r \in Robots, w \in ZoneAisles : Leave(r, w)
    \/ \E w \in ZoneAisles : ReleaseFine(w)
    \/ \E z \in Zones : ReleaseZone(z)
    \/ \E r \in Robots, w \in ZoneAisles : AdminAdmit(r, w)
    \/ \E r \in Robots, w \in ZoneAisles : AdminEvict(r, w)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

CapacityOK == \A w \in ZoneAisles : Cardinality(occupancy[w]) <= Cap

nl:
A warehouse robot fleet moves through aisles that each sit inside a zone, and each aisle can hold only a bounded number of robots at once. Under the normal hierarchical-lock discipline a robot must first take the zone's coarse lock, then the aisle's fine lock, and only then enter the aisle, which succeeds only if the aisle is below its capacity. A robot may leave an aisle, and locks may be released, with a zone lock released only once all its aisle fine locks are free. A privileged supervisor may override the lock hierarchy: it can admit a robot directly into an aisle without any locks, and it can evict a robot from an aisle, logging each override. Crucially, even the supervisor's direct admit still respects the aisle's physical capacity. The fleet controller must guarantee that no aisle ever holds more robots than its capacity.
SAFETY PROPERTY: Every aisle always holds a number of robots less than or equal to its fixed capacity.

A wildfire drone surveillance swarm maintains a single shared coverage register, and write access is serialized by a circulating ring token: only the drone currently holding the token may commit a write. A drone prepares a write by recording the register version it observed, and these prepared writes are buffered and delivered to the committer in any order over an unreliable mesh, so writes are not applied in the order they were prepared. A prepared write commits only if the drone that prepared it currently holds the token and the version it observed still matches the live version; committing advances the register version by one and logs the applied write together with the version it produced. A prepared write whose observed version is stale is rejected. The token is passed around the ring so different drones get their turn. Correctness requires that no committed write is lost: two distinct applied writes can never share the same produced version.
SAFETY PROPERTY: No two distinct applied writes are logged at the same register version, so no committed coverage update is silently lost.

    /\ votes' = {}

    /\ votes' = {}

    /\ mode[r] = "idle"
    /\ candidate' = r
    /\ mode' = [mode EXCEPT ![r] = "waiting"]
    /\ votes' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED bay

    /\ candidate # NONE
    /\ v \notin votes
    /\ votes' = votes \cup {v}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<mode, candidate, bay>>

    /\ Cardinality(votes) >= Quorum
    /\ bay = NONE
    /\ mode' = [mode EXCEPT ![candidate] = "using"]
    /\ bay' = candidate
    /\ candidate' = NONE
    /\ votes' = {}

    /\ mode' = [mode EXCEPT ![candidate] = "idle"]
    /\ candidate' = NONE
    /\ votes' = {}

    /\ mode' = [mode EXCEPT ![r] = "idle"]
    /\ bay' = NONE
    /\ UNCHANGED <<candidate, votes>>

    \/ \E v \in Voters : Ballot(v)
    \/ Grant
    \/ Abandon
    \/ \E r \in Robots : Release(r)

CONSTANTS
    Robots = {r1, r2}
    Voters = {v1, v2, v3}
    Quorum = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT AtMostOneUsing
nl:
A warehouse robot fleet shares a single charging bay that only one robot may use at a time. Access is decided by quorum voting: a robot is nominated for the bay, and the fleet's relay voters cast ballots for the nominee. Because ballots travel over a noisy channel they arrive in any order, so votes are counted as they land rather than in the order cast. When a quorum of ballots has been gathered for the nominee and no robot is currently using the bay, the nominee is granted the bay and switches to using it; nominations can also be abandoned. A robot using the bay eventually releases it and returns to idle. Each robot is therefore in one of three modes: idle, waiting after nomination, or using the bay, and the bay separately records which robot currently occupies it, kept in agreement with that robot's using mode. The safety-critical requirement is mutual exclusion: at most one robot may be in the using mode at any instant.
SAFETY PROPERTY: At most one robot is ever in the using mode, so no two robots occupy the charging bay simultaneously.
